status: Frozen before the storage rollback experiment
contract: Store.transaction: All writes inside are atomic; vectors are rolled back with rows.
hypothesis: For a file-backed store before its periodic vector flush, aborting a later transaction can replace previously committed vector state with the older on-disk snapshot while SQL correctly retains the earlier committed change.
design: Two prior committed changes (delete an existing chunk; insert a new chunk) crossed with three storage conditions (default file-backed deferred persistence; file-backed explicit flush after committed change; in-memory). Six deterministic controls, one execution each, not an incidence estimate.
fixture: Two synthetic orthogonal 4-dimensional vectors and inert chunk text; initial store explicitly flushed before the tested committed change.
interruption: Raise an authored RuntimeError inside a later transaction after adding a third temporary row/vector. No process crash, concurrency or physical failure.
oracle: All public SQL rows, all public vector IDs/values and public vector search output immediately before abort must equal those after abort. The temporary row/vector must be absent. In file-backed conditions, close/reopen is observed separately.
runtime: Previously isolated Python 3.12.14 / numpy 2.2.6 / scipy 1.15.3 qualification environment. Not the paper's full pinned model runtime.
source_policy: Use acquired upstream Python bytes unchanged. No custom embeddings/model classes, no weights, no hosted calls and no source patch.
scope: Native SQLite storage transaction semantics only, not full Lightfoot deletion, generated-answer leakage, parameter forgetting, physical erasure, novel transaction algorithms or field-wide priority. No comparator efficacy claim beyond explicit-flush/in-memory controls.
